question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: A node is a map whose t entry is text. A tree or nested element that is not a node (none, bool, f64, text, list, a map without t, a map whose t is not text) throws. A node whose t is not exactly (case-sensitive) one of TAGS throws, including a t that names a built-in member of a host object ("constructor", "__proto__", "toString"). A node holding any entry its tag's row of NODE-KEYS does not list throws. A listed entry that is missing throws wherever the tag's rule reads it.
none -> none.

text -> v, which must be text, with a cu entry that must be exactly "utf8" or "utf16" (else throws). With "utf8", v must be well-formed (no unpaired surrogate code unit), else throws. With "utf16", v must NOT be well-formed (it holds at least one unpaired surrogate; js only), else throws: a well-formed text has one spelling, cu "utf8", so a "utf16" empty text, ASCII text or properly paired astral text throws. The result is v.
bool -> v, which must be a bool, else throws.
"undefined" (the js extension's tag) -> the absent value (js only).
bigint (the js extension's tag) -> v must be DECIMAL text, else throws; the result is that integer as a big integer (js only), never a host number, at any magnitude; no range check.

i64 and u64 -> v must be DECIMAL text, else throws. Its integer n must lie in the tag's range, else throws: i64 -2^63 <= n <= 2^63-1, u64 0 <= n <= 2^64-1. When -2^53 <= n <= 2^53, BOTH bounds inclusive -> the f64 equal to n; otherwise -> n as a big integer (js only).

bytes -> v must be text matching BASE64-CANONICAL, else throws, and the final group's unused low bits must be zero, else throws: "base64:AR==" and "base64:AQJ=" throw, "base64:AQ==" decodes to the one byte 1. The result (js only) is the bytes the base64 after the prefix encodes; "base64:" alone is no bytes.

f64 -> v must be text (else throws; its content is a display hint and is never compared with bits: "banana" and the empty text are accepted CITED FIDELITY package). bits must be text of exactly 16 characters, each a digit or a lowercase a-f, nothing before or after, else throws. The result is the binary64 whose IEEE-754 bit pattern, sign bit first, those digits spell; 8000000000000000 is -0, 7ff0000000000000 and fff0000000000000 are the infinities. A NaN pattern is accepted only as exactly 7ff8000000000000; every other NaN pattern (any other payload, the sign bit set) throws.
list and tuple (identical) -> v must be a list, else throws; each element is decoded by R1 in order; the result is the list of results. A tuple's arity is not checked.

map -> v must be a list, else throws. Each entry must be a list of exactly two elements, else throws. The first is decoded by R1 and must decode to text (only a text node does, so a utf16 key is one holding a lone surrogate), else throws; it is the key. A key equal to an earlier key throws. Each key must be strictly greater than the previous key under KEY-ORDER, else throws. The second element decoded by R1 is the value. Every key is an ordinary key of the result, including "__proto__" and the names of a host object's built-in members. Entry order is not part of the result (a json map is unordered).

record -> v must be a list, else throws. Each field must be a list of exactly two elements whose first is well-formed text (the name, NOT decoded; a name holding an unpaired surrogate throws), else throws; the second decoded by R1 is the value. A name equal to an earlier name throws. Field order is NOT checked (the encoder writes the SIG's order, which the decoder does not know). The result is a map from names to values, every name an ordinary key as in R11. CITED FIDELITY package

throw -> msg must be text, else throws (a missing msg too). The result is a VALUE, never a throw: the map with exactly one entry, named __threw, whose value is msg (the empty msg included), at the top level and nested alike. Decoding a throw node returns that map; it does not raise.
A throw anywhere in the tree aborts the whole call: there is no partial result. A throw's message is a display hint, never part of the contract.

Nesting cap, MAX-VALUE-DEPTH = 100: the root is at depth 0; every element of a list or tuple, every map key and every map value, and every record value is one deeper than the node holding it (a record name is not a node). A position at depth greater than 100 throws, whatever it holds (a node, a non-node, a throw node); depth 100 itself is legal: a chain of 101 nested nodes (the innermost at depth 100) decodes, a chain of 102 throws. Only positions that exist count: an empty list, map, tuple or record at depth 100 decodes, while one holding any element, entry or field throws. A throw node at depth 100 decodes to its one-entry map (R13), whose msg then sits one value deeper than the cap. CITED FIDELITY package
"none" | "bool" | "text" | "f64" | "i64" | "u64" | "bytes" | "list" | "tuple" | "map" | "record" | "throw" | "undefined" | "bigint"
"none" "undefined"                           | t
"bool" "bigint" "bytes" "i64" "u64"          | t, v
"list" "tuple" "map" "record"                | t, v
"text"                                       | t, v, cu
"f64"                                        | t, v, bits
"throw"                                      | t, msg
"0"                                                       | zero
an optional "-", then a digit 1-9, then any ASCII digits  | that integer
anything else: "-0", a "+", a leading zero ("007"), whitespace or a line break anywhere (a trailing one included), an exponent, a fraction, a hex prefix, a non-text v, the empty text | throws
the prefix "base64:" (required, exactly once)                                     |
then zero or more groups of 4 characters of the standard alphabet A-Z a-z 0-9 + / |
then optionally ONE final padded group: 2 alphabet characters and "==", or 3 alphabet characters and "=" |
anything else: no prefix, the url-safe alphabet - _, whitespace or a line break anywhere, a missing or extra "=", a group of 1 character | throws
